sources.entry: DBeaver - Universal database tool and SQL client.

summary.one_liner: DBeaver is a free, multi-platform database tool and SQL client for developers, DBAs and analysts that works with any JDBC- or ODBC-accessible database.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a desktop database tool with a schema editor, SQL editor, data editor, ER diagrams, data export/import/migration, SQL execution plans, database administration tools, dashboards, a spatial data viewer, proxy and SSH tunnelling, and a custom driver editor. It states that the community edition ships with over 100 database drivers and that any database with a JDBC or ODBC driver can be used. An AI Chat view is included for generating, analysing and optimizing SQL and understanding database structure. The application is mostly Java, built on Eclipse RCP and OSGi, and it bundles OpenJDK 25 in its distributions. The README also mentions CloudBeaver (a web version on the same platform) and dbvr (a CLI tool).
use_cases: query and edit data in MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server or Oracle
visualize table relationships with ER diagrams
export, import or migrate data between databases
generate or optimize SQL queries with an AI chat
connect to databases through SSH tunnels or proxies
how_to_run: Download an installer or archive from the official website or GitHub releases
Run the installer and launch the DBeaver app icon
Or unzip the archive and run `dbeaver` from the command line
notable: Over 100 community database drivers out of the box, plus any JDBC or ODBC database
Integrated AI chat with database-structure context and dynamic tools
Community version has 130+ OSGi plugins, with model plugins shared with CloudBeaver
Bundles its own JRE, which can be replaced by swapping the jre directory
Daily Early Access builds are available
caveats: Many NoSQL and cloud databases, plus native Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama and other AI providers, are only in the commercial PRO versions
Community AI providers are limited to OpenAI (custom endpoints) and Copilot
Requires Java; OpenJDK 25 is bundled but can be replaced
